docs.title: WTV Documentation
docs.text: Welcome to the WTV documentation. This project provides tools for ion selection in mass spectrometry data based on the WTV-2.0 algorithm.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Command-line interface (CLI) for easy usage
  • Library functions for programmatic access
  • Support for MSP file format
  • Support for libraries with retention times or retention indices
  • Configurable parameters for different use cases

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: uv sync --all-extras

docs.title: Running the CLI
docs.text: uv run wtv-cli --msp_path input.msp --outpath ./output --mz_min 35 --mz_max 400

docs.text: This project is based on the original work by Honglun Yuan et al., published in WTV_2.0.

  • wtv.ion_selection - Core ion selection algorithms

from pathlib import Path

docs.title: API Reference: Ion Selection
docs.text: This document describes the ion selection functions in wtv.ion_selection.

docs.title: run_ion_selection
docs.text: Main function for performing ion selection on MSP files.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description msp_file_path Path Required Path to the input MSP file output_directory Path Required Directory to save the output files mz_min float 0 Minimum m/z value mz_max float inf Maximum m/z value rt_window float | None None Retention window for finding nearby compounds, in the units of retention_field; defaults to RT_WINDOW_DEFAULT (0.1 minutes) for retention times and to RT_INDEX_WINDOW_DEFAULT (40 index units) for retention indices min_ion_intensity_percent float 5 Minimum ion intensity percentage min_ion_num int 3 Minimum number of ions required prefer_mz_threshold float 150 Preferred m/z threshold similarity_threshold float 0.85 Similarity threshold for compound matching fr_factor float 2 Fragment ratio factor retention_time_max float inf Maximum retention time or index value retention_field str "retention_time" Field to use for retention data: "retention_time" or "retention_index"; raises MissingRetentionDataError when the selected field carries no usable values

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path
from wtv.ion_selection import run_ion_selection

run_ion_selection(
    msp_file_path=Path("input.msp"),
    output_directory=Path("output"),
    mz_min=35,
    mz_max=400,
    rt_window=0.1,
    min_ion_intensity_percent=7,
    min_ion_num=2,
    prefer_mz_threshold=60,
    similarity_threshold=0.85,
    fr_factor=2.0,
    retention_time_max=68.80,
)

docs.title: dot_product_distance
docs.text: Calculate the dot product distance between two vectors.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Description p np.ndarray First vector q np.ndarray Second vector

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: • float: Dot product distance between the two vectors (0 to 1)

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
import numpy as np
from wtv.similarity import dot_product_distance

p = np.array([1, 2, 3])
q = np.array([4, 5, 6])
score = dot_product_distance(p, q)
print(f"Similarity score: {score}")

docs.title: read_msp
docs.text: Reads an MSP file and returns metadata and retention time data using matchms.

docs.title: Parameters

docs.title: Returns

  • Dictionary of compound names to ion intensities
  • DataFrame with columns 'Name' and 'RT'

docs.text:
from wtv.utils import read_msp

meta, rt_data = read_msp("input.msp")
print(meta.keys())  # Compound names
print(rt_data)      # Retention times

docs.title: resolve_rt_window
docs.text: Select the retention window when the caller left it unset. An explicitly supplied window is returned unchanged; otherwise a default is chosen. Because retention times and retention indices live on different scales there is no single scale-free default: for retention_field="retention_index" the function returns RT_INDEX_WINDOW_DEFAULT and logs a warning asking the user to review the value against the index spread of their data. A substituted retention-time default is logged at INFO level, because a window that is orders of magnitude too wide is invisible in the output otherwise.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description rt_window float or None Required User supplied window; None selects a default retention_field str Required Field used for retention data

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: • float: The window to apply, in the units of retention_field

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from wtv.utils import resolve_rt_window

resolve_rt_window(None, "retention_index")  # -> 40.0 (logs a warning)
resolve_rt_window(None, "retention_time")   # -> 0.1
resolve_rt_window(1.5, "retention_index")   # -> 1.5

docs.title: MissingRetentionDataError
docs.text: Exception (subclass of ValueError) raised by get_rt_data - and therefore by read_msp, load_data, and parse_spectra - when the selected retention field is absent from the spectrum metadata or holds no numeric value for any spectrum. The message names the retention field that was found instead, when one exists, and states the option to rerun with (for example --retention_field retention_index). The CLI catches this error, logs the message, and exits with code 1 instead of raising a traceback.

docs.title: RT_WINDOW_DEFAULT
docs.text: Module constant, 0.1. Default retention window in minutes, used by resolve_rt_window when retention_field="retention_time" and no explicit rt_window was given. It replaces the previous default of one minute, which on a fast GC gradient spans tens of compounds and turns the neighbour-aware selection into an all-compared-against-all search.

docs.title: RT_INDEX_WINDOW_DEFAULT
docs.text:
Module constant, 40.0. Default retention window in retention-index units, used by resolve_rt_window when retention_field="retention_index" and no explicit rt_window was given. Retention indices span hundreds to thousands of units, so neither a minute-scale value nor the retention-time default can be reused numerically.

The two constants are calibrated against each other through the gradient slope. The test libraries that carry both fields give the conversion directly:

File Conversion (least squares fit) Index units per minute test_data/sample_data/chunk_0.msp RI = 345.09 · RT + 269.80 345 test_data/sample_data/ei_spectra.msp RI = 324.95 · RT + 355.50 325

At that slope, 40 index units are 0.12 minutes - the same physical window as RT_WINDOW_DEFAULT. Both values are starting points; tune them to the retention spread, gradient, and peak widths of your own data.

docs.title: RETENTION_FIELDS
docs.text: Module constant, ("retention_time", "retention_index"): the retention metadata fields understood by the package. These are the valid values for the retention_field parameters and for the CLI --retention_field option.

docs.title: CLI Usage
docs.text: The WTV CLI provides an easy way to perform ion selection on mass spectrometry data.

docs.title: Basic Command
docs.text:
wtv-cli --msp_path input.msp --outpath output --mz_min 35 --mz_max 400 ...

When using uv:

uv run wtv-cli --msp_path input.msp --outpath output ...

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description Default --msp_path Path to the input MSP file. Required --outpath Directory to save the output files. Required --mz_min Minimum m/z value. 35 --mz_max Maximum m/z value. 400 --rt_window Retention window for finding nearby compounds, in the units of --retention_field. 0.1 (retention_time) / 40.0 (retention_index) --min_ion_intensity_percent Minimum ion intensity percentage. 7 --min_ion_num Minimum number of ions. 2 --prefer_mz_threshold Preferred m/z threshold. 60 --similarity_threshold Similarity threshold. 0.85 --fr_factor FR factor. 2.0 --retention_time_max Maximum retention time or index value. inf --retention_field Field to use for retention data; one of retention_time or retention_index. GC-MS libraries often provide a retention index instead of a retention time. retention_time

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
Run ion selection with default parameters:

wtv-cli \
    --msp_path input.msp \
    --outpath ./output \
    --mz_min 35 \
    --mz_max 400 \
    --rt_window 0.1 \
    --min_ion_intensity_percent 7 \
    --min_ion_num 2 \
    --prefer_mz_threshold 60 \
    --similarity_threshold 0.85 \
    --fr_factor 2.0 \
    --retention_time_max 68.80

docs.title: Custom Parameters
docs.text:
Adjust parameters for your specific data:

wtv-cli \
    --msp_path my_data.msp \
    --outpath ./results \
    --mz_min 50 \
    --mz_max 500 \
    --rt_window 0.15 \
    --similarity_threshold 0.9

docs.title: Retention-Indexed Libraries
docs.text:
Some GC-MS libraries annotate compounds with a retention index instead of a retention time. Select the field the input file provides:

wtv-cli \
    --msp_path library_with_ri.msp \
    --outpath ./output \
    --retention_field retention_index

--rt_window is interpreted in the units of --retention_field. If it is not given, 0.1 is used for retention times (minutes) and 40.0 retention-index units for retention indices (a warning is logged). The two numbers describe the same physical window: the test libraries that carry both fields measure 325-345 index units per minute, so 40 index units are about 0.12 minutes.

Choosing the window is a matter of matching it to the distance between compounds that genuinely co-elute, not to the length of the gradient. A window of whole minutes on a fast GC gradient is the failure mode to avoid: test_data/sample_data/chunk_0.msp holds 87 compounds between 2.59 and 8.14 minutes, a median of 0.04 minutes apart, so --rt_window 1.0 returns 34.7 neighbours for the average compound and --rt_window 2.0 returns 61.4, out of 87 - the selection degenerates into comparing every compound against every other. At the 0.1 default the same figure is 4.4. Both defaults are starting points, not validated optima: check them against the retention spread of your own library. An explicit --rt_window always overrides the default.

If the selected field is absent from the file or holds no numeric value for any spectrum, execution stops with an error message that names the retention field actually found and the --retention_field value to rerun with, and the CLI exits with code 1.

docs.title: Using with uv
docs.text:
If you installed with uv, run:

uv run wtv-cli --msp_path input.msp --outpath ./output --mz_min 35 --mz_max 400

docs.title: Output
docs.text: The CLI generates an MSP file in the specified output directory containing the filtered spectra based on the ion selection algorithm.

docs.title: Using uv (Recommended)
docs.text:
1. Install uv if you haven't already: ```bash # Using pip pip install uv

# Or using Homebrew on macOS brew install uv

# Or using curl curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh ```

  1. Clone the repository: bash git clone https://github.com/RECETOX/wtv.git cd wtv

  2. Sync dependencies and create virtual environment: bash uv sync --all-extras

This will: - Create a virtual environment in .venv - Install all dependencies including dev and docs extras - Make the wtv-cli command available

docs.title: Common uv Commands
docs.text: Command Description uv sync Sync dependencies (install packages) uv sync --all-extras Install all optional dependencies uv run <command> Run a command in the virtual environment uv add <package> Add a new dependency uv build Build distribution packages

docs.title: Using pip
docs.text:
1. Install the library directly from PyPI: bash pip install wtv

  2. For development, clone the repository and install in editable mode: bash git clone https://github.com/RECETOX/wtv.git cd wtv pip install -e ".[dev,docs]"

docs.title: Verify Installation
docs.text:
Run the following command to verify the installation:

wtv-cli --help

You should see the CLI help message with available options.

docs.title: Basic Example
docs.text:
Run ion selection using the run_ion_selection function:

from pathlib import Path
from wtv.ion_selection import run_ion_selection

run_ion_selection(
    msp_file_path=Path("input.msp"),
    output_directory=Path("output"),
    mz_min=35,
    mz_max=400,
    rt_window=0.1,
    min_ion_intensity_percent=7,
    min_ion_num=2,
    prefer_mz_threshold=60,
    similarity_threshold=0.85,
    fr_factor=2.0,
    retention_time_max=68.80,
)

docs.title: run_ion_selection
docs.text:
Main function for performing ion selection on MSP files.

Parameters: - msp_file_path (Path): Path to the input MSP file - output_directory (Path): Directory to save output - mz_min (float): Minimum m/z value (default: 0) - mz_max (float): Maximum m/z value (default: infinity) - rt_window (float): Retention window for finding nearby compounds, in the units of retention_field (default: 0.1 minutes, or 40 retention-index units) - min_ion_intensity_percent (float): Minimum ion intensity percentage (default: 5) - min_ion_num (int): Minimum number of ions required (default: 3) - prefer_mz_threshold (float): Preferred m/z threshold (default: 150) - similarity_threshold (float): Similarity threshold for compound matching (default: 0.85) - fr_factor (float): Fragment ratio factor (default: 2) - retention_time_max (float): Maximum retention time (default: infinity)

Example:

from pathlib import Path
from wtv.ion_selection import run_ion_selection

# Run with custom parameters
run_ion_selection(
    msp_file_path=Path("data/sample.msp"),
    output_directory=Path("results"),
    mz_min=50,
    mz_max=500,
    rt_window=0.15,
    similarity_threshold=0.9,
)

docs.title: generate_ion_combinations
docs.text:
Generate optimal ion combinations for compounds.

Parameters: - min_ion_intensity_percent: Minimum ion intensity percentage - min_ion_num: Minimum number of ions - prefer_mz_threshold: Preferred m/z threshold - similarity_threshold: Similarity threshold - fr_factor: Fragment ratio factor - RT_data: DataFrame with retention time data - matrix: DataFrame with ion intensities - rt_window: Retention window, in the units of the retention field

Example:

from wtv.utils import load_data
from wtv.ion_selection import generate_ion_combinations

# Load data
RT_data, matrix = load_data(Path("input.msp"), mz_min=35, mz_max=400)

# Generate ion combinations
combinations = generate_ion_combinations(
    min_ion_intensity_percent=7,
    min_ion_num=2,
    prefer_mz_threshold=60,
    similarity_threshold=0.85,
    fr_factor=2.0,
    RT_data=RT_data,
    matrix=matrix,
    rt_window=0.1,
)

docs.title: Data Loading
docs.text:
from wtv.utils import load_data, read_msp, create_ion_matrix

RT_data, matrix = load_data(Path("input.msp"), mz_min=35, mz_max=400)

docs.text:
from wtv.utils import write_msp

# Write filtered spectra to MSP file
write_msp(ion_rt_df, Path("output"), Path("input.msp"))

docs.text:
The library uses Python's logging module. To see detailed logs:

import logging

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)

from wtv.ion_selection import run_ion_selection
run_ion_selection(...)

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text: How the version is stored, how to bump it, and how a release reaches PyPI.

docs.title: Where the version lives
docs.text:
The version is declared in exactly one place: [project].version in pyproject.toml (PEP 621). Everything else is derived from it.

Place How it gets the version pyproject.toml, [project].version declared by hand - the only source of truth wtv.__version__ read from the installed distribution metadata (importlib.metadata) wtv-cli --version the same metadata, through wtv.__version__ uv.lock, the name = "wtv" package written by uv when the lock is refreshed git tag v<version> created when the release is cut

Never edit the version in uv.lock by hand - refresh the lock with uv lock. tests/test_version.py fails if the declared version, the installed metadata and the lock file disagree, so a mismatch cannot go unnoticed.

docs.title: Version policy
docs.text:
The project adheres to semantic versioning, as recorded at the top of the changelog.

Change Bump Changelog section Bug fix with no change in behaviour patch Fixed New backwards-compatible functionality, a new CLI option or API parameter minor Added A change to what the same input produces, e.g. a rescaled default parameter minor Changed Removed or renamed option or parameter, dropped Python version, new output layout major Changed / Removed

Because a changed default can change a user's results, it is never a patch bump. Whatever the bump, the change and its reason belong in the changelog.

docs.title: Bumping the version
docs.text:
Bumping is done with bump-my-version, configured in [tool.bumpversion] in pyproject.toml. It reads the current version from the PEP 621 metadata, so there is no second copy of the version to keep in sync, and it rewrites pyproject.toml and uv.lock together. It does not commit or tag - the release branch goes through a pull request like any other change.

  1. Start from a clean, up-to-date main. The tool refuses a tree with modified tracked files, which is why the setup for a release is committed before the bump itself. Untracked files are not refused, so do not expect it to catch stray data files for you.

    bash git checkout main && git pull git checkout -b rel/<version>

  2. Preview what would change - <part> is major, minor or patch:

    bash uv run bump-my-version bump <part> --dry-run --verbose

    Two targets should be listed: pyproject.toml:project.version, printed as a PEP 621 pointer rather than a bare filename, and uv.lock. Anything else in that list is a mistake in [tool.bumpversion].

  3. Apply the bump:

    bash uv run bump-my-version bump <part>

  4. Refresh the environment, so the installed metadata and the lock agree:

    bash uv sync --all-extras --dev

    Without this step the editable install still reports the previous version and tests/test_version.py fails. That failure is the intended signal, not a problem with the test.

    Pass the extras. dev and docs are optional-dependency extras rather than uv dependency groups, so a bare uv sync removes them - it uninstalls pytest, ruff, black, isort and bump-my-version, and the verification below then fails for the wrong reason.

  5. Verify:

    bash uv lock --locked # the lock agrees with pyproject.toml uv run pytest # the whole suite, including the version checks uv run ruff check . uv build # dist/wtv-<version>-*.whl and .tar.gz carry the new version uv run wtv-cli --version

  6. Move the [Unreleased] changelog block under a ## [<version>] - YYYY-MM-DD heading and open a fresh, empty [Unreleased]. Stamp the date of preparation and correct it if the release slips.

  7. Commit the two rewritten files plus the changelog, push the branch and open a pull request against main. CI runs the tests and the build on three operating systems.

docs.title: Cutting the release
docs.text:
After the release pull request is merged:

git checkout main && git pull
git tag -a v<version> -m "Release <version>"
git push origin v<version>

-a makes an annotated tag. The tags up to v0.2.1 are lightweight, so this deliberately changes the convention: an annotated tag records who tagged it and when, and git describe ignores lightweight tags unless given --tags.

Then publish a GitHub release for that tag. .github/workflows/publish.yml runs on the published event, builds with uv build and uploads with uv publish --token $PYPI_API_TOKEN. The workflow can also be started by hand (Run workflow) if the release already exists and publishing failed.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] The bump level matches the policy above, not merely the size of the diff
  • [ ] The dry run lists only pyproject.toml:project.version and uv.lock
  • [ ] The environment was refreshed with uv sync --all-extras --dev, so the verification ran with the tools installed
  • [ ] Every user-visible change since the previous tag is in the changelog section for this release, including its reason and any limitation
  • [ ] uv lock --locked, uv run pytest, uv run ruff check . and uv build pass
  • [ ] The release pull request is merged into main before the tag is pushed
  • [ ] The GitHub release notes match the changelog section
  • [ ] After publishing, the new version installs from PyPI: pip install wtv==<version> && wtv-cli --version

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Publishing requires a published GitHub release; pushing a tag alone publishes nothing.
  • The bioconda recipe advertised by the README badge lives outside this repository and is not covered by this workflow.
  • Changelog entries are written by hand; nothing generates them from merged pull requests.
  • The uv.lock entry under [tool.bumpversion] matches the shape of the lock file uv writes today. If that shape changes, the bump stops with an error (ignore_missing_version = false) rather than half-bumping the release.
  • dev is a published extra, not a uv dependency group, so bump-my-version and the other release tools appear in Requires-Dist ... extra == "dev" and pip install wtv[dev] pulls them. Moving the whole dev extra to a [dependency-groups] section would keep them out of the published metadata and make a bare uv sync install them; that changes every uv sync --all-extras call in the README, the docs and CI, so it is a change for its own branch.

docs.title: Library Usage
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path
